LATIN TIMES: "Sheinbaum Delivers Her Second Report Card — Here's the Fine Print Mexican Diaspora Families Need"
August 29, 2026 | 🟢

A rare US-outlet explainer that centers the diaspora, not the drug war. It relays Sheinbaum's numbers straight: irregular migration down ~97.5% from its peak, remittances near 3.5% of GDP. The squeeze it names is on the US side — Trump's 1% remittance excise tax, live since Jan. 1, hitting cash and money-order transfers home.

For 40 million people of Mexican descent in the US, it frames Washington's banking rules — not Mexico City's — as the thing to watch.

• migration "fallen roughly 97.5% from its peak"
• remittances "close to 3.5% of Mexico's entire economic output"
banner: Trump's 1% tax on money sent home

BORDERREPORT/CNN: "Key financial operator for Sinaloa cartel's Chapitos faction arrested, DEA says"
August 30, 2026 | 🟡

The capture happened in Mexicali, by Mexican forces — security chief Omar García Harfuch announced the arrest of Salvador "El Gusano" Díaz. The headline credits "DEA says." DEA administrator Terry Cole called it work "on both sides of the border"; the byline puts one side first.

Harfuch said the operation came from Mexican intelligence and investigative work — a line that lands below the DEA in the US retelling.

• headline attribution: "DEA says"
• "sustained intelligence... on both sides of the border"
banner: Mexican capture, credited to the DEA

CBS/AFP: Tigers, jaguars, bison among 135 exotic animals "found in raid on fuel smugglers"
August 28, 2026 | 🟡

CBS leads with a cartel zoo — Bengal tigers, a camel, an American bison. The actual operation: Mexican marines dismantling a huachicol fuel-theft ring in Tamaulipas, seizing 18,000 gallons of stolen diesel, pumps and tanks. The exotic animals were incidental; the fuel bust — cartels' #2 revenue stream per the US Treasury — was the point.

The raid was Mexican forces' work, but no Mexican official is quoted; the spectacle gets the headline, the security win gets a clause.

• "rescued Bengal tigers, mandrills, hyenas and even a camel"
• victims "fed dead or alive to tigers"
banner: Fuel-theft bust reframed as cartel zoo

🇲🇽🚢 <u>MEXICO'S TARIFFS CUT CHINESE IMPORTS 28% — EBRARD DOUBLES DOWN</u>

Mexican imports from China fell 28.4% between January and May after Economy Secretary Marcelo Ebrard's tariffs hit 1,463 product lines from countries with no trade deal with Mexico: footwear collapsed 59%, light vehicles 35%, textiles 13.9%. Ebrard is betting the drop reactivates Mexican industry — footwear, textiles, apparel, appliances, toys — rather than just rerouting the same imports through other ports, per El Financiero.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>MILEI'S BOT-FARM OPERATIVE PLOTTED TO "BLOW UP" MEXICO'S ELECTIONS</u>

Fernando Cerimedo — co-founder of La Derecha Diario and a former adviser to Javier Milei — planned to "reventar" Mexico's coming elections out of hatred for Sheinbaum, his ex-partner told the press: "He told me he was going to blow up the elections, yes, because he detests the president." Arrested in La Paz on August 20, Bolivian authorities seized cash in multiple currencies and a "bot farm" built to manufacture social-media trends and mass fake engagement.
banner: BOT-FARM PLOT TO WRECK MEXICO ELECTIONS

🇲🇽🏭 <u>MEXICO IS PLANNING ITS ECONOMY AGAIN — NOT JUST MANAGING IT</u>

Plan México's 15 Welfare Development Poles are pulling real capital into the country's interior: a 16-billion-peso pole in Hidalgo, a 10.1-billion-peso DEWA project promising 5,000+ jobs, and Cruz Azul's cooperative reactivating its Tula plant for 3 million tons of cement and 14,000 jobs, with the México–Pachuca train due in 2027. As Contralínea's Carolina Hernández puts it, "administration keeps the engine running; planning decides where the country flies" — a break from decades of leaving development to the market.

🇲🇽🌽 <u>MEXICO FARMS A TENTH OF ITS LAND — AND IMPORTS THE REST</u>

Mexico has 36 million hectares of arable land but cultivates just 20 million, irrigating only 6 million (barely 1.5 million by drip), while 56% of the territory shows soil degradation and roughly 35% of food produced is wasted, per Contralínea. Pablo Moctezuma frames it plainly: real food sovereignty means breaking dependence on multinational agrochemical giants and putting idle, fertile land to work — "¡Tierra y libertad!" as a present-tense demand, not a museum slogan.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>MEXICO STANDS BY BACHELET FOR UN CHIEF — EVEN AFTER CHILE WALKED</u>

Mexico and Brazil are keeping Michelle Bachelet's candidacy for UN Secretary-General alive after Chile's government pulled its own sponsorship in March and she slipped in the Security Council's second straw poll. Sheinbaum called her "a woman with a lot of experience who seeks peace in the world," backing a Latin American woman for the top UN post on a platform of human rights and multilateralism — while the region's right abandons one of its own.
banner: MEXICO BACKS BACHELET FOR UN CHIEF

text:
🇲🇽🛡️ <u>MEXICO PUTS FOREIGN CAPITAL UNDER NATIONAL-SECURITY LOCK</u>

Sheinbaum sent Congress a reform giving a beefed-up National Foreign Investment Commission — now seated with Defense, the Navy, intelligence and the treasury's financial-crimes unit — veto power over any foreign buyer seeking more than 49% of Mexican firms in energy, mining, ports, data centers, semiconductors, AI or defense. The state gets 60 days to green-light, condition, or block a deal on national-security grounds. The US has screened foreign money in its strategic sectors for decades; Mexico is now claiming the same right over its own ground.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Mexican forces seize an arsenal of 6,000+ explosives in Chihuahua</u>

Federal forces seized a cartel arsenal of more than 6,000 explosive devices in Chihuahua — part of coordinated operations that also struck Sinaloa, netting an encampment, 33 long guns, cocaine, marijuana and detentions. Mexican intelligence, Mexican forces: the war-grade stockpiles left by the neoliberal era, dismantled on Mexican soil. (La Jornada)
